Q 37:62–70 · Vol. 4, pp. 45–47

Verses 62 to 70

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Is that a better accommodation or the tree of zaqqum? (62) Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers (63) Indeed, it is a tree that comes forth from the bottom of the Hellfire (64) Its fruit is as if it were the heads of devils (65) And indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it (66) Then indeed, they will have after it a mixture of scalding water (67) Then indeed, their return will be to the Hellfire (68) Indeed they found their fathers astray (69) So they hurry in their footsteps (70)
أَذلِكَ خَيْرٌ نُزُلاً أَمْ شَجَرَةُ الزَّقُّومِ (62) إِنَّا جَعَلْناها فِتْنَةً لِلظَّالِمِينَ (63) إِنَّها شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ فِي أَصْلِ الْجَحِيمِ (64) طَلْعُها كَأَنَّهُ رُؤُسُ الشَّياطِينِ (65) فَإِنَّهُمْ لَآكِلُونَ مِنْها فَمالِؤُنَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ (66) ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْها لَشَوْباً مِنْ حَمِيمٍ (67) ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لَإِلَى الْجَحِيمِ (68) إِنَّهُمْ أَلْفَوْا آباءَهُمْ ضالِّينَ (69) فَهُمْ عَلى آثارِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ (70)
Vol. 4, p. 46
The story of the believer and his companion is complete; then He returns to the mention of the known provision, saying: "Is that" provision "a better accommodation," that is, a better yield, "or the tree of zaqqum?" The original sense of "nuzul" is surplus and profit in food; one says: "food abundant in nuzul"; so it was borrowed for what accrues from something. The yield of the known provision is pleasure and joy, while the yield of the tree of zaqqum is pain and distress. "Nuzulan" is accusative as specification, and you may make it a circumstantial accusative, as you say: "Does the palm tree yield better as unripe dates or as ripe dates?" That is, the known provision is the accommodation of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire have as their accommodation the tree of zaqqum, so which of them is better as an accommodation? "Nuzul" is what is prepared «1» for one who alights at a place of provision. From it comes the "inzal" of soldiers' provisions, as one says of what is set up for a house's dweller: "sakan." «2» The meaning of the former: the known provision has an accommodation and the tree of zaqqum has an accommodation, so which is better as an accommodation? And it is known that there is no good in the tree of zaqqum, but since the believers chose what led to the known provision and the disbelievers chose what led to the tree of zaqqum, this was said to them as a reproach for their bad choice. "A trial for the wrongdoers": an ordeal and punishment for them in the Hereafter; or a testing of them in this world, for they said: How can there be a tree in the Fire when fire burns trees? So they denied it. It has been read "nabita." "From the bottom of the Hellfire": it is said that its place of growth is in the depths of Hell and its branches rise to its levels. And "tal'" belongs to the palm, and was borrowed for what comes forth from the tree of zaqqum of its fruit: either as a verbal metaphor or a conceptual one; and it was likened to the heads of devils to indicate its extreme repulsiveness and ugliness of appearance, because the devil is hateful and ugly in people's natures, as they believe he is pure evil unmixed with good, so of the ugly in form they say: "as if it were the face of a devil," "as if the head of a devil." And when artists depict him they bring his image in the ugliest and most terrifying form they can, just as they believed the angel to be pure good with no evil in him, so they liken beautiful form to him. God, the Exalted, said: "This is not a human being; this is nothing but a noble angel." This is an imaginative simile. It is also said: the devil is a crested serpent of exceedingly ugly and frightful appearance. It is also said that there is a tree called "al-ustun," rough, foul-smelling, bitter, of repellent shape, whose fruit is called
تمت قصة المؤمن وقرينه، ثم رجع إلى ذكر الرزق المعلوم فقال أَذلِكَ الرزق خَيْرٌ نُزُلًا أى خير حاصلا أَمْ شَجَرَةُ الزَّقُّومِ وأصل النزل: الفضل والربع في الطعام، يقال: طعام كثير النزل، فاستعير للحاصل من الشيء، وحاصل الرزق المعلوم: اللذة والسرور، وحاصل شجرة الزقوم: الألم والغم، وانتصاب نزلا على التمييز، ولك أن تجعله حالا، كما تقول: أثمر النخلة خير بلحا أم رطبا؟ يعنى أنّ الرزق المعلوم نزل أهل الجنة. وأهل النار نزلهم شجرة الزقوم، فأيهما خير في كونه نزلا. والنزل: ما يقال «1» للنازل بالمكان من الرزق. ومنه إنزال الجند لأرزاقهم، كما يقال لما يقام لساكن الدار: السكن «2» . ومعنى الأوّل: أنّ للرزق المعلوم نزلا، ولشجر الزقوم نزلا، فأيهما خير نزلا. ومعلوم أنه لا خير في شجرة الزقوم، ولكن المؤمنين لما اختاروا ما أدى إلى الرزق المعلوم، واختار الكافرون ما أدى إلى شجرة الزقوم، قيل لهم ذلك توبيخا على سوء اختيارهم فِتْنَةً لِلظَّالِمِينَ محنة وعذابا لهم في الآخرة. أو ابتلاء لهم في الدنيا، وذلك أنهم قالوا: كيف يكون في النار شجرة والنار تحرق الشجر، فكذبوا. وقرئ: نابتة فِي أَصْلِ الْجَحِيمِ قيل: منبتها في قعر جهنم، وأغصانها ترتفع إلى دركاتها: والطلع للنخلة، فاستعير لما طلع من شجرة الزقوم من حملها: إما استعارة لفظية، أو معنوية، وشبه برءوس الشياطين دلالة على تناهيه في الكراهة وقبح المنظر، لأنّ الشيطان مكروه مستقبح في طباع الناس، لاعتقادهم أنه شر محض لا يخلطه خير، فيقولون في القبيح الصورة: كأنه وجه شيطان، كأنه رأس شيطان. وإذا صوّره المصورون: جاءوا بصورته على أقبح ما يقدر وأهوله، كما أنهم اعتقدوا في الملك أنه خير محض لا شر فيه، فشبهوا به الصورة الحسنة. قال الله تعالى ما هذا بَشَراً إِنْ هذا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ وهذا تشبيه تخييلى. وقيل: الشيطان حية عرفاء لها صورة قبيحة المنظر هائلة جدا. وقيل: إنّ شجرا يقال له الأستن خشنا منتنا مرا منكر الصورة، يسمى ثمره:
Vol. 4, p. 47
"heads of devils." The Arabs named this fruit "heads of devils" only intending one of the two similes, but after being so named it became a third basis with which it is likened. "From it" means from the tree, that is, from its fruit, "and fill their bellies," because of the intense hunger that overcomes them, or they are compelled to eat it though they hate it, as a category of torment; then when they are full thirst overcomes them and they are given to drink of "ghassaq" or pus, "mixed" [shawb: its blend] "with scalding water" that scorches their faces and cuts their intestines, as He said in describing the drink of the people of Paradise: "and its mixture is of Tasnim." It has been read "la-shuuban," with damma, which is a name for what is mixed in, and the first is naming by the verbal noun.
رؤوس الشياطين. وما سمت العرب هذا الثمر برءوس الشياطين إلا قصدا إلى أحد التشبيهين، ولكنه بعد التسمية بذلك رجع أصلا ثالثا يشبه به مِنْها من الشجرة، أى من ظلعها فَمالِؤُنَ بطونهم، لما يغلبهم من الجوع الشديد، أو يقسرون على أكلها وإن كرهوها، ليكون بابا من العذاب، فإذا شبعوا غلبهم العطش فيسقون شرابا من غساق أو صديد، شوبه: أى مزاجه مِنْ حَمِيمٍ يشوى وجوههم ويقطع أمعاءهم، كما قال في صفة شراب أهل الجنة وَمِزاجُهُ مِنْ تَسْنِيمٍ وقرئ: لشوبا، بالضم، وهو اسم ما يشاب به، والأوّل تسمية بالمصدر.
Question
If you say: What is the meaning of the particle of delay (thumma) in His saying "Then indeed they will have after it a mixture" and in His saying "Then indeed their return"?
فإن قلت: ما معنى حرف التراخي في قوله ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمْ عَلَيْها لَشَوْباً وفي قوله ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ؟
Answer
I say: in the first there are two aspects: one, that they fill their bellies from the tree of zaqqum, which is hot, burning their bellies and making them thirsty, so they are given drink only after being full, as torment by that thirst, then they are given what is hotter, namely the drink mixed with scalding water. The second: that He mentioned the food with its repulsiveness and loathsomeness, then mentioned the drink as even more repulsive and loathsome, so He used "thumma" to indicate the distance of the state of the drink from the state of the food, and the difference of its description from the description of that in exceeding it. As for the second: they are taken from their abodes and stations in Hell, which are the levels in which they were housed, to the tree of zaqqum, so they eat until they are full and are given drink after that, then return to their levels, and the sense of delay in that is clear. It has also been read: "thumma inna munqalabahum," "thumma inna masirahum," "thumma inna munfadhahum ila al-jahim." He explained their deserving to fall into all these hardships by their imitating fathers in religion, following them in error, and abandoning the following of evidence. "Ihra'" is intense hurrying, as if they are being urged on strongly. It is also said: hurrying with a resemblance to trembling.
قلت: في الأوّل وجهان، أحدهما: أنهم يملئون البطون من شجر الزقوم، وهو حارّ يحرق بطونهم ويعطشهم، فلا يسقون إلا بعد ملىّ تعذيبا بذلك العطش، ثم يسقون ما هو احرّ وهو الشراب المشوب بالحميم. والثاني: أنه ذكر الطعام بتلك الكراهة والبشاعة، ثم ذكر الشراب بما هو أكره وأبشع، فجاء بثم للدلالة على تراخى حال الشراب عن حال الطعام ومباينة صفته لصفته في الزيادة عليه. ومعنى الثاني: أنهم يذهب بهم عن مقارّهم ومنازلهم في الجحيم، وهي الدركات التي أسكنوها إلى شجرة الزقوم، فيأكلون إلى أن يتملئوا، ويسقون بعد ذلك، ثم يرجعون إلى دركاتهم، ومعنى التراخي في ذلك بين: وقرئ: ثم إن منقلبهم، ثم إن مصيرهم، ثم إن منفذهم إلى الجحيم: علل استحقاقهم للوقوع في تلك الشدائد كلها بتقليد الآباء في الدين، واتباعهم إياهم على الضلال، وترك اتباع الدليل. والإهراع: الإسراع الشديد، كأنهم يحثون حثا. وقيل: إسراع فيه شبه بالرعدة.

Q 37:71–74 · Vol. 4, p. 47

Verses 71 to 74

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And certainly, before them, most of the former peoples went astray (71) And We had certainly sent among them warners (72) So see how was the end of those who were warned (73) Except the chosen servants of God (74)
وَلَقَدْ ضَلَّ قَبْلَهُمْ أَكْثَرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (71) وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا فِيهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ (72) فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ (73) إِلاَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ الْمُخْلَصِينَ (74)
Vol. 4, p. 47
"And certainly before them went astray": before your people, the Quraysh. "Warners": prophets who cautioned them about consequences. "Those who were warned": those who were warned and cautioned, that is, all of them were destroyed, "except the servants of God" who believed among them and devoted their religion sincerely to God, or whom God chose for His religion, according to the two readings.
وَلَقَدْ ضَلَّ قَبْلَهُمْ قبل قومك قريش. مُنْذِرِينَ أنبياء حذروهم العواقب. الْمُنْذَرِينَ الذين أنذروا وحذروا، أى أهلكوا جميعا إِلَّا عِبادَ اللَّهِ الذين آمنوا منهم وأخلصوا دينهم لله، أو أخلصهم الله لدينه على القراءتين.
18
Q 37:75–82 · Vol. 4, pp. 47–48

Verses 75 to 82

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And Noah certainly called upon Us, and excellent were the Responders (75) And We saved him and his family from the great distress (76) And We made his descendants those who remained (77) And We left for him [a good reputation] among the later generations (78) Peace upon Noah among the worlds (79) Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good (80) Indeed, he was of Our believing servants (81) Then We drowned the others (82)
وَلَقَدْ نادانا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ الْمُجِيبُونَ (75) وَنَجَّيْناهُ وَأَهْلَهُ مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ (76) وَجَعَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ الْباقِينَ (77) وَتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرِينَ (78) سَلامٌ عَلى نُوحٍ فِي الْعالَمِينَ (79) إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ (80) إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبادِنَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (81) ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا الْآخَرِينَ (82)
Vol. 4, p. 48
Having mentioned the sending of warners among past nations and the evil end of those warned, He follows that with the mention of Noah and his calling upon Him when he despaired of his people. The lam entering "ni'ma" is the answer to an omitted oath, and the one specified for praise is omitted; its implication is: "By God, excellent are the Responders, We." The plural is evidence of grandeur and majesty. The meaning: We answered him in the best answering, bringing it to his intended aim and desire of helping him against his enemies and taking vengeance on them in the most thorough way. "Those who remained": they are the ones who remained alone when others perished; for it is reported that everyone who was with him in the ark died except his offspring; or they are those who remained, multiplying, until the Day of Resurrection. Qatada said: all people are of the descendants of Noah. Noah ﷺ had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth. Shem is the father of the Arabs, Persians and Romans (Byzantines). Ham is the father of the blacks from the East to the West. Japheth is the father of the Turks, and of Gog and Magog. "And We left for him among the later generations" of nations this phrase, which is: "Peace upon Noah," meaning that they greet him with salutation and pray for him; it is from quoted speech, as you say: "I recited a surah We have revealed."
لما ذكر إرسال المنذرين في الأمم الخالية وسوء عاقبة المنذرين، أتبع ذلك ذكر نوح ودعائه إياه حين أيس من قومه، واللام الداخلة على نعم جواب قسم محذوف، والمخصوص بالمدح محذوف تقديره: فو الله لنعم المجيبون نحن، والجمع دليل العظمة والكبرياء. والمعنى: إنا أجبناه أحسن الإجابة، وأوصلها إلى مراده وبغيته من نصرته على أعدائه والانتقام منهم بأبلغ ما يكون هُمُ الْباقِينَ هم الذين بقوا وحدهم وقد فنى غيرهم، فقد روى أنه مات كل من كان معه في السفينة غير ولده. أو هم الذين بقوا متناسلين إلى يوم القيامة. قال قتادة: الناس كلهم من ذرية نوح. وكان لنوح عليه السلام ثلاثة أولاد: سام، وحام، ويافث. فسام أبو العرب، وفارس، والروم. وحام أبو السودان من المشرق إلى المغرب. ويافث أبو الترك ويأجوج ومأجوج وَتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرِينَ من الأمم هذه الكلمة، وهي: سَلامٌ عَلى نُوحٍ يعنى يسلمون عليه تسليما، ويدعون له، وهو من الكلام المحكي، كقولك: قرأت سورة أنزلناها.
Question
If you say: What is the meaning of His saying "among the worlds"?
فإن قلت: فما معنى قوله فِي الْعالَمِينَ؟
Answer
I say: its meaning is a prayer for the permanence of this greeting among all of them and that none of them be without it, as if it were said: God has established the salutation to Noah and perpetuated it among the angels and the two weighty races [humans and jinn], who all greet him. He explained that Noah's ﷺ being repaid with that exalted honor, the preservation of his mention and the salutation of the worlds upon him to the end of time, was because he was a doer of good, then explained his being a doer of good by his being a believing servant, to show you the majesty of the station of faith, and that it is the utmost of the attributes of praise and exaltation, and to make you desire acquiring it and increasing in it.
قلت: معناه الدعاء بثبوت هذه التحية فيهم جميعا، وأن لا يخلو أخد منهم منها، كأنه قيل: ثبت الله التسليم على نوح وأدامه في الملائكة والثقلين يسلمون عليه عن آخرهم. علل مجازاة نوح عليه السلام بتلك التكرمة السنية من تبقية ذكره، وتسليم العالمين عليه إلى آخر الدهر بأنه كان محسنا، ثم علل كونه محسنا بأنه كان عبدا مؤمنا، ليريك جلالة محل الإيمان، وأنه القصارى من صفات المدح والتعظيم، ويرغبك في تحصيله والازدياد منه.
19
Q 37:83–87 · Vol. 4, pp. 48–49

Verses 83 to 87

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And indeed, among his kind was Abraham (83) When he came to his Lord with a sound heart (84) When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship? (85) Is it falsehood — gods other than God — that you desire? (86) Then what is your thought about the Lord of the worlds?" (87)
وَإِنَّ مِنْ شِيعَتِهِ لَإِبْراهِيمَ (83) إِذْ جاءَ رَبَّهُ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ (84) إِذْ قالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ ماذا تَعْبُدُونَ (85) أَإِفْكاً آلِهَةً دُونَ اللَّهِ تُرِيدُونَ (86) فَما ظَنُّكُمْ بِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (87)
Vol. 4, p. 48
"Among his kind (shi'a)": of those who followed him in the fundamentals of religion even if their laws differed; or who followed him in steadfastness in God's religion and patience with the deniers. It is possible that there was agreement between their two laws in most things. From Ibn Abbas ؓ both: of the people of his religion and upon his way; and between Noah and Abraham there were only two prophets: Hud and Salih. Between Noah and Abraham were two thousand six hundred and forty years.
مِنْ شِيعَتِهِ ممن شايعه على أصول الدين وإن اختلفت شرائعهما. أو شايعه على التصلب في دين الله ومصابرة المكذبين. ويجوز أن يكون بين شريعتيهما اتفاق في أكثر الأشياء. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: من أهل دينه وعلى سنته، وما كان بين نوح وإبراهيم إلا نبيان: هود، وصالح. وكان بين نوح وإبراهيم ألفان وستمائة وأربعون سنة.
Question
If you say: To what is the adverbial clause attached?
فإن قلت: بم تعلق الظرف؟
Answer
I say: to the sense of following in "shi'a," meaning: and among those who followed him in his religion and piety, when Abraham came to his Lord with a sound heart; or to an omitted verb: "Remember." "With a sound heart": from all the ailments of hearts. It is also said: from polytheism, but there is no sense in specifying because it is unrestricted, and some ailments are no more deserving than others, so it embraces them all.
قلت: بما في الشيعة من معنى المشايعة، يعنى: وإن ممن شايعه على دينه وتقواه حين جاء ربه بقلب سليم لإبراهيم. أو بمحذوف وهو: اذكر بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ من جميع آفات القلوب. وقيل: من الشرك، ولا معنى للتخصيص لأنه مطلق، فليس بعض الآفات أولى من بعض فيتناولها كلها.
Question
If you say: What is the meaning of coming to his Lord with his heart?
فإن قلت: ما معنى المجيء بقلبه ربه؟
Answer
I say: its meaning is that he devoted his heart purely to God, and that was known of him, so He made
قلت: معناه أنه أخلص لله قلبه، وعرف ذلك منه فضرب
Vol. 4, p. 49
the coming a figure for that. "Is it falsehood": an object of purpose, its implication being: "Do you desire gods other than God as falsehood?" He put the object before the verb for emphasis, and put the object of purpose before the direct object, because it was most important to him to confront them with the fact that they were in falsehood and error in their polytheism. It is also possible that "ifkan" is an object, meaning: do you desire falsehood by it? Then He explained falsehood with His saying "gods other than God," in that they are falsehood in themselves. It is also possible that it is a circumstantial accusative, meaning: do you desire gods besides God while lying? "Then what is your thought" about the One who is truly worthy of worship, for whoever is Lord of the worlds deserves to be worshipped by them, so that you left worshipping Him for worshipping idols; the meaning is: no thought or supposition can conceive of anything that would deter from worshipping Him. Or: "Then what is your thought of Him," what sort of thing is He among things, that you made the idols peers to Him? Or: "Then what is your thought about Him, what will He do to you and how will He punish you when you have worshipped another?"
المجيء مثلا لذلك أَإِفْكاً مفعول له، تقديره: أتريدون آلهة من دون الله إفكا، وإنما قدّم المفعول على الفعل للعناية، وقدّم المفعول له على المفعول به، لأنه كان الأهمّ عنده أن يكافحهم بأنهم على إفك وباطل في شركهم. ويجوز أن يكون إفكا مفعولا، يعنى: أتريدون به إفكا. ثم فسر الإفك بقوله آلِهَةً دُونَ اللَّهِ على أنها إفك في أنفسها. ويجوز أن يكون حالا، بمعنى: أتريدون آلهة من دون الله آفكين فَما ظَنُّكُمْ بمن هو الحقيق بالعبادة، لأنّ من كان ربا للعالمين استحق عليهم أن يعبدوه، حتى تركتم عبادته إلى عبادة الأصنام: والمعنى: أنه لا يقدّر في وهم ولا ظنّ ما يصدّ عن عبادته. أو فما ظنكم به أى شيء هو من الأشياء، حتى جعلتم الأصنام له أندادا. أو فما ظنكم به ماذا يفعل بكم وكيف يعاقبكم وقد عبدتم غيره؟
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 49
1. (1) . "Kanat qanati la talinu li-ghamizin / fa-alanaha al-isbahu wa al-imsa'u / fa-da'awtu rabbi bi-al-salamati jahidan / li-yusihhani fa-idha al-salamatu da'un" by Labid ibn Rabi'a al-Amiri. "Al-qanat" is the spear, which he borrowed for his uprightness or strength by explicit metaphor, while softness and pressing are the embellishment. "Al-ghamiz" is one who presses with the hand. It is possible that the metaphor is an allegorical one in the compound, describing his strength in the time of youth, then the weakness of the state of old age through the succession of times upon him, and that he sought an extension of his term, which was the cause of his waning.
1. (1) . كانت قناتي لا تلين لغامز
…. فألانها الإصباح والإمساء فدعوت ربى بالسلامة جاهدا
…. ليصحنى فإذا السلامة داء للبيد بن ربيعة العامري، والقناة: الرمح، استعارها لاقامته أو قوته على طريق التصريح، والليونة والغمز: ترشيح. والغمزى: الحبى باليد ويجوز أن الاستعارة تمثيلية في المركب، يصف قوته زمن الشباب، ثم ضعف حال المشيب بتتابع الأزمان عليه، وأنه تطلب فسحة الأجل، فكانت سبب اضمحلاله.
20
Q 37:88–90 · Vol. 4, pp. 49–50

Verses 88 to 90

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Then he cast a glance at the stars (88) And said, "Indeed, I am ill" (89) So they turned away from him, departing (90)
فَنَظَرَ نَظْرَةً فِي النُّجُومِ (88) فَقالَ إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ (89) فَتَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ مُدْبِرِينَ (90)
Vol. 4, p. 49
"At the stars": in the science of the stars, or in its books or its rulings. It is related of one of the kings that he was asked about his heart's desire and said: a beloved to look at, a needy person to look after, and a book to look into. The people were astrologers, so he made them imagine that he deduced from a sign in the science of the stars that he would fall ill, "and said, Indeed I am ill": I am on the verge of illness, namely plague, which was the commonest of illnesses among them, and they feared contagion; so that they would disperse from him, they fled from him to their festival and left him in the house of the idols with no one with him, and he did to the idols what he did.
فِي النُّجُومِ في علم النجوم أو في كتابها أو في أحكامها، وعن بعض الملوك أنه سئل عن مشتهاه فقال: حبيب أنظر إليه، ومحتاج أنظر له، وكتاب أنظر فيه. كان القوم نجامين، فأوهمهم أنه استدل بأمارة في علم النجوم على أنه يسقم فَقالَ إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ إنى مشارف للسقم وهو الطاعون، وكان أغلب الأسقام عليهم، وكانوا يخافون العدوى ليتفرقوا عنه، فهربوا منه إلى عيدهم وتركوه في بيت الأصنام ليس معه أحد، ففعل بالأصنام ما فعل.
Question
If you say: How was it permissible for him to lie?
فإن قلت: كيف جاز له أن يكذب؟
Answer
I say: some people have permitted it in military stratagem and dissimulation, pleasing a spouse, and reconciling between the contending and the estranged. The correct view is that lying is forbidden except when one speaks equivocally and ambiguously, and what Abraham ﷺ said was an equivocal expression, and he intended by it that whoever has death upon his neck is ill. From it comes the proverb: "Health is enough of a disease." And the saying of Labid: "So I called upon my Lord for health, striving, / that He make me well, and lo, health was a disease." «1» A man once died suddenly and people gathered around him saying: He died while healthy; and a Bedouin said: Is one healthy when death is upon his neck? It is also said: he meant: I am sick at heart because of your disbelief.
قلت: قد جوّزه بعض الناس في المكيدة في الحرب والتقية، وإرضاء الزوج والصلح بين المتخاصمين والمتهاجرين. والصحيح: أن الكذب حرام إلا إذا عرّض وورّى، والذي قاله إبراهيم عليه السلام: معراض من الكلام، ولقد نوى به أن من في عنقه الموت سقيم. ومنه المثل: كفى بالسلامة داء. وقول لبيد: فدعوت ربى بالسّلامة جاهدا … ليصحّنى فإذا السّلامة داء «1» وقد مات رجل فجأة فالتف عليه الناس وقالوا: مات وهو صحيح، فقال أعرابى: أصحيح من الموت في عنقه. وقيل: أراد: إنى سقيم النفس لكفركم.
Vol. 4, p. 50
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages

1. (1) . "Kanat qanati la talinu li-ghamizin / fa-alanaha al-isbahu wa al-imsa'u / fa-da'awtu rabbi bi-al-salamati jahidan / li-yusihhani fa-idha al-salamatu da'un" by Labid ibn Rabi'a al-Amiri. "Al-qanat" is the spear, which he borrowed for his uprightness or strength by explicit metaphor, while softness and pressing are the embellishment. "Al-ghamiz" is one who presses with the hand. It is possible that the metaphor is an allegorical one in the compound, describing his strength in the time of youth, then the weakness of the state of old age through the succession of times upon him, and that he sought an extension of his term, which was the cause of his waning.

…. فألانها الإصباح والإمساء فدعوت ربى بالسلامة جاهدا
…. ليصحنى فإذا السلامة داء للبيد بن ربيعة العامري، والقناة: الرمح، استعارها لاقامته أو قوته على طريق التصريح، والليونة والغمز: ترشيح. والغمزى: الحبى باليد ويجوز أن الاستعارة تمثيلية في المركب، يصف قوته زمن الشباب، ثم ضعف حال المشيب بتتابع الأزمان عليه، وأنه تطلب فسحة الأجل، فكانت سبب اضمحلاله.

1. (1) . His statement "when he drove him (hadahu)": that is, drove him along. Stated in al-Sihah. (Ayn)
2. . His statement "and the elite (al-'illiyya)": that is, the great ones. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «إذا حداه» أى ساقه. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)

21
Q 37:91–93 · Vol. 4, p. 50

Verses 91 to 93

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Then he turned to their gods and said, "Do you not eat? (91) What is [wrong] with you that you do not speak?" (92) Then he turned upon them, striking with the right hand (93)
فَراغَ إِلى آلِهَتِهِمْ فَقالَ أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ (91) ما لَكُمْ لا تَنْطِقُونَ (92) فَراغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْباً بِالْيَمِينِ (93)
Vol. 4, p. 50
"Then he turned to their gods": he went to them secretly, from the "rawgha" of the fox; "to their gods": to their idols, which were gods in their claim, as in His saying: "Where are My partners?" "Do you not eat? What is [wrong] with you that you do not speak?" is mockery of them and of their being lower than the state of their worshippers. "Then he turned upon them": he came at them in stealth, as if he said: so he struck them "a blow," because "ragha 'alayhim" means he struck them; or "faragha 'alayhim yadribuhum darban"; or "faragha 'alayhim darban" meaning striking. It has also been read "saf'qan" and "safqan," whose meaning is striking. And the meaning of "striking with the right hand" is a severe, powerful blow, because the right is the stronger and harder of the two limbs. It is also said: with force and firmness; and also: because of the oath, which is His saying "By God, I will surely plot against your idols."
فَراغَ إِلى آلِهَتِهِمْ فذهب إليها في خفية، من روغة الثعلب، إلى آلهتهم: إلى أصنامهم التي هي في زعمهم آلهة، كقوله تعالى: أين شركائى؟ أَلا تَأْكُلُونَ ما لَكُمْ لا تَنْطِقُونَ استهزاء بها وبانحطاطها عن حال عبدتها فَراغَ عَلَيْهِمْ فأقبل عليهم مستخفيا، كأنه قال: فضربهم ضَرْباً لأن راغ عليهم بمعنى ضربهم. أو فراغ عليهم يضربهم ضربا. أو فراغ عليهم ضربا بمعنى ضاربا. وقرئ: صفقا وسفقا، ومعناهما: الضرب. ومعنى ضربا بِالْيَمِينِ ضربا شديدا قويا، لأن اليمين أقوى الجارحتين وأشدّهما. وقيل: بالقوّة والمتانة: وقيل: بسبب الحلف، وهو قوله تَاللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنامَكُمْ.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 50
1. (1) . His statement "when he drove him (hadahu)": that is, drove him along. Stated in al-Sihah. (Ayn)
2. . His statement "and the elite (al-'illiyya)": that is, the great ones. (Ayn)

2. . قوله «والعلية» أى العظماء. (ع)
22
Q 37:94 · Vol. 4, pp. 50–51

Verse 94

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Then they came to him, hastening (94)
فَأَقْبَلُوا إِلَيْهِ يَزِفُّونَ (94)
Vol. 4, p. 50
"Yazifun" means hurrying, from the "zafif" of ostriches. And "yuzifun": from "azaffa," when one enters into zafif; or from "azaffahu," when he drives him to zafif, that is: some of them urge on others. And "yuzaffun," in the passive form, meaning they are driven to zafif. And "yazifun," from "wazafa yazifu" when he hurried. And "yazfun": from "zafahu" when he drove him along «1», as if some of them drive others because of their haste toward him.
يَزِفُّونَ يسرعون، من زفيف النعام. ويزفون: من أزفّ، إذا دخل في الزفيف. أو من أزفه، إذا حمله على الزفيف، أى: يزفّ بعضهم بعضا. ويزفون، على البناء للمفعول، أى: يحملون على الزفيف. ويزفون، من وزف يزف إذا أسرع. ويزفون: من زفاه إذا حداه «1» ، كأن بعضهم يزفوا بعضا لتسارعهم إليه،
Question
If you say: Between this and His saying, "They said, 'Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers.' They said, 'We heard a youth mention them, who is called Abraham,'" there is an apparent contradiction, since here He mentions that they turned away from him fearing contagion, and when they saw him breaking them they came toward him rushing to restrain him and fall upon him, whereas there He mentions that they asked about the breaker, until they were told: "We heard Abraham disparaging them, so perhaps he is the breaker"; so in one they saw him breaking them, in the other they deduced from his disparagement that he was the breaker.
فإن قلت: بين هذا وبين قوله تعالى قالُوا مَنْ فَعَلَ هذا بِآلِهَتِنا إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ، قالُوا سَمِعْنا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقالُ لَهُ إِبْراهِيمُ كالتناقض حيث ذكر هاهنا أنهم أدبروا عنه خيفة العدوى، فلما أبصروه يكسرهم أقبلوا إليه متبادرين ليكفوه ويوقعوا به، وذكر ثم أنهم سألوا عن الكاسر، حتى قيل لهم: سمعنا إبراهيم يذمهم، فلعله هو الكاسر، ففي أحدهما أنهم شاهدوه يكسرها، وفي الآخر: أنهم استدلوا بذمه على أنه الكاسر.
Answer
I say: there are two aspects. One: that those who saw him and rushed toward him were a handful of them, not the mass of them and their elders; so when the mass and the elite «2» returned from their festival to the house of the idols to eat the food they had placed with them for blessing, and saw them broken, they were repelled by that and asked: Who has done this to them? Then those handful did not denounce him with an explicit denunciation, but by way of allusion and hint in their saying "We heard a youth mention them," for some reason that restrained them. The second: that he broke them and left without anyone being aware of it, and their approach to him hastening came after their return from their festival and their asking about the breaker. And their saying: "They said, 'Then bring him before the eyes of the people.'"
قلت: فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يكون الذين أبصروه وزفوا إليه نفرا منهم دون جمهورهم وكبرائهم، فلما رجع الجمهور والعلية «2» من عيدهم إلى بيت الأصنام ليأكلوا الطعام الذي وضعوه عندها لتبرك عليه ورأوها مكسورة اشمأزوا من ذلك، وسألوا: من فعل هذا بها؟ ثم لم ينم عليه أولئك النفر نميمة صريحة، ولكن على سبيل التورية والتعريض بقولهم «سمعنا فتى يذكرهم» لبعض الصوارف. والثاني: أن يكسرها ويذهب ولا يشعر بذلك أحد، ويكون إقبالهم إليه يزفون بعد رجوعهم من عيدهم وسؤالهم عن الكاسر. وقولهم: قالوا فأتوا به على أعين الناس.
Vol. 4, p. 51
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 50
1. (1) . His statement "when he drove him (hadahu)": that is, drove him along. Stated in al-Sihah. (Ayn)
2. . His statement "and the elite (al-'illiyya)": that is, the great ones. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «إذا حداه» أى ساقه. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قوله «والعلية» أى العظماء. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 51
1. (1) . Mahmud said: "He means: He created you and what you make of idols, as in His saying 'Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them.' If you say: How can one single thing be created by God, the Exalted, and made by them? He answered that this is as it is said: the carpenter made the door
... until he said:
... and in that is a dissolving and severing of the construction, as if you made it a verbal-noun particle." End of his words. Ahmad said: When God's flood comes, the flood of Ma'qil goes; so we say: it is necessary to take it as a verbal-noun particle, and that is because they did not worship these idols in respect of their being unformed stones; for were it so, they would not have cooperated in forming them, nor singled out one stone over another for their worship, which shows that they worship them only with respect to their shapes and forms, which are the effect of their work; so in reality they worshipped their own work, and the argument against them is proper, namely that they are like it, even though the object of worship is the worshipper's acquisition and work; so it has become apparent that the argument stands against them, on the assumption that "ma" is a verbal-noun particle, in the clearest and most eloquent way. When that is established, let his speech be followed by refutation. As for his saying that it is relative, and that what is meant by their making them is making their shapes, it contradicts the apparent sense, because it needs the omission of an annexed word in a place of despair, its implication being: "God created you and what you make the shape and form of," unlike the explanation of the Sunnis, which needs no omission whatsoever. Then, if the object of worship is made the substance itself, how can their reproach be matched with the explanation that the object of worship is the worshipper's work, while agreeing that the substances of the idols are not their work? What is their work, namely the shape, is not their object of worship on this interpretation, and what is their object of worship, namely the substance of the idol, is not their work, so for him there is no stable footing in the object of worship being, on his interpretation, the work of the worshipper, whereas on what we have established it becomes clear. As for his saying that the correspondence between "what you carve" and "what you do" comes apart on the Sunnis' interpretation, it is not correct, for we may take the first as a verbal-noun particle also, and that in truth they worshipped their carving, because these idols, being stones before carving, they did not worship; when they worked carving upon them they worshipped them; so in truth they worshipped nothing but their carving which is their work, so the correspondence is achieved, and the obligation on this basis is more eloquent and firmer. Had it been as he said, the argument would have stood for them, and they would have said, as al-Zamakhshari says, confronting His saying "God created you and what you do," by saying: No, and no honor; God does not create what we do, for we only did the shaping and forming and this God did not create; and they would have found a pretext to plunge into the argument; but God insists that we have the conclusive argument and they have the empty falsehoods. So this is a constraint, indeed a bridle, for whoever opposes the Sunna, a shackle on his neck, a hamstringing at his shoulder, and a blow upon his hand, until he returns to the truth, repentant, and acknowledges his error, penitent.
2. . His statement "If you say, why do you reject (anakarta)?": perhaps: "why did you reject (lam ankarta)." (Ayn) [.....]
3. . His statement "as the Mujbira say": he means the Sunnis, since they held that there is no creator but God, so He is the creator of the servant's act, while the Mu'tazila say that the servant is the creator of his own act, making the servant God's partner in creatorship, though they named themselves the people of justice and divine oneness. They said: if God were the creator of the servant's act, His punishing the servant for acts of disobedience would be injustice rather than justice. The Sunnis said: He punishes him for them as He rewards him for obedience, because of the servant's acquisition and choice in both, so there is no injustice; but the Mu'tazila did not look into divine oneness with complete scrutiny, nor did they gain complete insight into its proofs. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قال محمود: «يعنى خلقكم وما تعملون من الأصنام، كقوله بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ فان قلت: كيف يكون الشيء الواحد مخلوقا لله تعالى معمولا لهم؟ وأجاب بأن هذا كما يقال: عمل النجار الباب
…. إلى أن قال:
…. وفي ذلك فك للنظم وتبتير كما لو جعلتها مصدرية» اه كلامه. قال أحمد: إذا جاء سيل الله ذهب سيل معقل، فنقول: يتعين حملها على المصدرية، وذلك أنهم لم يعبدوا هذه الأصنام من حيث كونها حجارة ليست مصورة، فلو كان كذلك لم يتعاونوا في تصويرها، ولا اختصوا بعبادتهم حجرا دون حجر، فدل أنهم إنما يعبدونها باعتبار أشكالها وصورها التي هي أثر عملهم، ففي الحقيقة أنهم عبدوا عملهم، وصلحت الحجة عليهم بأنهم مثله، مع أن المعبود كسب العابد وعمله، فقد ظهر أن الحجة قائمة عليهم على تقدير أن تكون ما مصدرية أوضح قيام وأبلغه، فإذا أثبت ذلك فليتتبع كلامه بالابطال. أما قوله أنها موصولة، وأن المراد بعملهم لها عمل أشكالها فمخالف للظاهر، فانه مفتقر إلى حذف مضاف في موضع اليأس يكون تقديره: والله خلقكم وما تعملون شكله وصورته، بخلاف توجيه أهل السنة فانه غير مفتقر إلى حذف البتة، ثم إذا جعل المعبود نفس الجوهر، فكيف يطابق توبيخهم ببيان أن المعبود من عمل العابد، مع موافقته على أن جواهر الأصنام ليست من عملهم؟ فما هو من عملهم وهو الشكل ليس معبودا لهم على هذا التأويل، وما هو معبودهم وهو جوهر الصنم ليس من عملهم، فلم يستقر له قرار في أن المعبود على تأويله من عمل العابد، وعلى ما قررناه يتضح. وأما قوله: إن المطابقة تنفك على تأويل أهل السنة بين ما ينحتون وما يعملون فغير صحيح، فان لنا أن نحمل الأولى على أنها مصدرية وأنهم في الحقيقة إنما عبدوا نحتهم، لأن هذه الأصنام وهي حجارة قبل النحت لم يكونوا يعبدونها، فلما عملوا فيها النحت عبدوها، ففي الحقيقة ما عبدوا سوى تحتهم الذي هو عملهم، فالمطابقة إذا حاصلة، والإلزام على هذا أبلغ وأمتن، ولو كان كما قال لقامت لهم الحجة، ولقالوا كما يقول الزمخشري مكافحين لقوله وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَما تَعْمَلُونَ بأن يقولوا: لا ولا كرامة، ولا يخلق الله ما نعمل نحن، لأنا إنما عملنا التشكيل والتصوير وهذا لم يخلقه الله، وكانوا يجدون الذريعة إلى اقتحام الحجة، ويأبى الله إلا أن تكون لنا الحجة البالغة ولهم الأكاذب الفارغة، فهذا إلزام بل إلجام لمن خالف السنة، وغل بعنقه، وعقر بكتفه، وضرب على يده، حتى يرجع إلى الحق آئبا، ويعترف بخطئه تائبا.
2. . قوله «فان قلت فما أنكرت» ؟ لعله: لم أنكرت. (ع) [.....]
3. . قوله «كما تقول المجبرة» يريد أهل السنة حيث ذهبوا إلى أنه لا خالق إلا الله، فهو الخالق لعمل العبد والمعتزلة يقولون: إن العبد هو الخالق لعمل نفسه، فجعلوا العبد شريكا لله في الخالقية، مع أنهم سموا أنفسهم أهل العدل والتوحيد، قالوا: لو كان الله هو الخالق لفعل العبد لكان تعذيبه للعبد على المعاصي ظلما لا عدلا، قال أهل السنة: يعذبه عليها كما يثيبه على الطاعة، لما له فيهما من الكسب والاختيار، فلا ظلم، لكن المعتزلة لم ينظروا في التوحيد تمام النظر، ولم يتبصروا في أدلته تمام التبصر. (ع)

Q 37:95–96 · Vol. 4, pp. 51–52

Verses 95 to 96

The verses as the commentary quotes them
He said, "Do you worship that which you carve? (95) While God created you and what you do?" (96)
قالَ أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ (95) وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَما تَعْمَلُونَ (96)
Vol. 4, p. 51
"While God created you and what you do": he means: He created you and what you make of idols, as in His saying: "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them" — that is, who created the idols.
وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَما تَعْمَلُونَ يعنى خلقكم وخلق ما تعملونه من الأصنام، كقوله بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ أى فطر الأصنام.
Question
If you say: How can one single thing be created by God and made by them, since He applied His creating and their making to all of them?
فإن قلت: كيف يكون الشيء الواحد مخلوقا لله معمولا لهم، حيث أوقع خلقه وعملهم عليها جميعا؟
Answer
I say: this is as it is said: "The carpenter made the door «1» and the chair," and "the goldsmith made the bracelet and the anklet"; what is meant is the making of the shapes and forms of these things, not their substances. The idols are substances and shapes: so the Creator of their substances is God, and the makers of their shapes are those who shape them by carving and by cutting away some of their parts until the shaping they want is complete.
قلت: هذا كما يقال: عمل النجار الباب «1» والكرسي، وعمل الصائغ السوار والخلخال، والمراد عمل أشكال هذه الأشياء وصورها دون جواهرها، والأصنام جواهر وأشكال، فخالق جواهرها الله، وعاملو أشكالها الذين يشكلونها بنحتهم وحذفهم بعض أجزائها، حتى يستوي التشكيل الذي يريدونه.
Question
If you say: Why do you reject «2» that "ma" is a verbal-noun particle rather than relative, so that the meaning is "God created you and your making," as the Mujbira say? «3»
فإن قلت: فما أنكرت «2» أن تكون ما مصدرية لا موصولة، ويكون المعنى: والله خلقكم وعملكم، كما تقول المجبرة «3» ؟
Answer
I say: the nearest thing by which this question is refuted, after its being refuted
قلت: أقرب ما يبطل به هذا السؤال بعد بطلانه
Vol. 4, p. 52
by the arguments of reason and the Book, is that the meaning of the verse rejects it with a clear rejection and shies from it with an evident aversion; for God, the Mighty and Majestic, argued against them that both the worshipper and the worshipped are God's creation, so how can a creature worship a creature, given that the worshipper of the two is the one who made the form and shape of the worshipped, and without him he could not have formed and shaped himself; and if you said: "God created you and created your work," He would not be arguing against them «1» nor would your speech have any correspondence. And another thing: His saying "what you do" is an exposition of His saying "what you carve," and the "ma" in "what you carve" is relative, about which there is no dispute, so it is not turned aside from its sister except by one who strains and is partisan to his school, without looking into the science of rhetoric or having insight into the construction of the Qur'an.
بحجج العقل والكتاب: أن معنى الاية يأباه إباء جليا، وينبو عنه نبوّا ظاهرا، وذلك أن الله عز وجل قد احتج عليهم بأنّ العابد والمعبود جميعا خلق الله، فكيف يعبد المخلوق المخلوق، على أن العابد منهما هو الذي عمل صورة المعبود وشكله، ولولاه لما قدر أن يصوّر نفسه ويشكلها، ولو قلت: والله خلقكم وخلق عملكم، ولم يكن محتجا عليهم «1» ولا كان لكلامك طباق. وشيء آخر: وهو أن قوله ما تَعْمَلُونَ ترجمة عن قوله ما تَنْحِتُونَ وما في ما تَنْحِتُونَ موصولة لا مقال فيها فلا يعدل بها عن أختها إلا متعسف متعصب لمذهبه، من غير نظر في علم البيان، ولا تبصر لنظم القرآن.
Question
If you say: Make it relative so that what you imposed does not bind me, and I mean: "and what you make of your deeds."
فإن قلت: اجعلها موصولة حتى لا يلزمني ما ألزمت، وأريد: وما تعملونه من أعمالكم.
Answer
I say: rather both constraints are on your neck, which can only be loosed by submission to the truth, because even if you make it relative, in your intending by it the deed you are not arguing against the polytheists, just as your state when you made it a verbal-noun particle; moreover you sever by that the link between "what you do" and "what you carve," in that you differ between what is meant by the two, intending by "what you carve" the substances which are the idols, and by "what you do" the abstractions which are the deeds, and in that is a dissolving and severing of the construction, as when you make it a verbal-noun particle.
قلت: بل الإلزامان في عنقك لا يفكهما إلا الإذعان للحق، وذلك أنك وإن جعلتها موصولة، فإنك في إرادتك بها العمل غير محتج على المشركين، كحالك وقد جعلتها مصدرية، وأيضا فإنك قاطع بذلك الصلة بين ما تعملون وما تنحتون، حيث تخالف بين المرادين بهما، فتريد بما تنحتون: الأعيان التي هي الأصنام، وبما تعملون: المعاني التي هي الأعمال، وفي ذلك فك النظم وتبتيره، كما إذا جعلتها مصدرية.

1. (1) . قال محمود: «يعنى خلقكم وما تعملون من الأصنام، كقوله بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ فان قلت: كيف يكون الشيء الواحد مخلوقا لله تعالى معمولا لهم؟ وأجاب بأن هذا كما يقال: عمل النجار الباب
…. إلى أن قال:
…. وفي ذلك فك للنظم وتبتير كما لو جعلتها مصدرية» اه كلامه. قال أحمد: إذا جاء سيل الله ذهب سيل معقل، فنقول: يتعين حملها على المصدرية، وذلك أنهم لم يعبدوا هذه الأصنام من حيث كونها حجارة ليست مصورة، فلو كان كذلك لم يتعاونوا في تصويرها، ولا اختصوا بعبادتهم حجرا دون حجر، فدل أنهم إنما يعبدونها باعتبار أشكالها وصورها التي هي أثر عملهم، ففي الحقيقة أنهم عبدوا عملهم، وصلحت الحجة عليهم بأنهم مثله، مع أن المعبود كسب العابد وعمله، فقد ظهر أن الحجة قائمة عليهم على تقدير أن تكون ما مصدرية أوضح قيام وأبلغه، فإذا أثبت ذلك فليتتبع كلامه بالابطال. أما قوله أنها موصولة، وأن المراد بعملهم لها عمل أشكالها فمخالف للظاهر، فانه مفتقر إلى حذف مضاف في موضع اليأس يكون تقديره: والله خلقكم وما تعملون شكله وصورته، بخلاف توجيه أهل السنة فانه غير مفتقر إلى حذف البتة، ثم إذا جعل المعبود نفس الجوهر، فكيف يطابق توبيخهم ببيان أن المعبود من عمل العابد، مع موافقته على أن جواهر الأصنام ليست من عملهم؟ فما هو من عملهم وهو الشكل ليس معبودا لهم على هذا التأويل، وما هو معبودهم وهو جوهر الصنم ليس من عملهم، فلم يستقر له قرار في أن المعبود على تأويله من عمل العابد، وعلى ما قررناه يتضح. وأما قوله: إن المطابقة تنفك على تأويل أهل السنة بين ما ينحتون وما يعملون فغير صحيح، فان لنا أن نحمل الأولى على أنها مصدرية وأنهم في الحقيقة إنما عبدوا نحتهم، لأن هذه الأصنام وهي حجارة قبل النحت لم يكونوا يعبدونها، فلما عملوا فيها النحت عبدوها، ففي الحقيقة ما عبدوا سوى تحتهم الذي هو عملهم، فالمطابقة إذا حاصلة، والإلزام على هذا أبلغ وأمتن، ولو كان كما قال لقامت لهم الحجة، ولقالوا كما يقول الزمخشري مكافحين لقوله وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَما تَعْمَلُونَ بأن يقولوا: لا ولا كرامة، ولا يخلق الله ما نعمل نحن، لأنا إنما عملنا التشكيل والتصوير وهذا لم يخلقه الله، وكانوا يجدون الذريعة إلى اقتحام الحجة، ويأبى الله إلا أن تكون لنا الحجة البالغة ولهم الأكاذب الفارغة، فهذا إلزام بل إلجام لمن خالف السنة، وغل بعنقه، وعقر بكتفه، وضرب على يده، حتى يرجع إلى الحق آئبا، ويعترف بخطئه تائبا.
2. . قوله «فان قلت فما أنكرت» ؟ لعله: لم أنكرت. (ع) [.....]
3. . قوله «كما تقول المجبرة» يريد أهل السنة حيث ذهبوا إلى أنه لا خالق إلا الله، فهو الخالق لعمل العبد والمعتزلة يقولون: إن العبد هو الخالق لعمل نفسه، فجعلوا العبد شريكا لله في الخالقية، مع أنهم سموا أنفسهم أهل العدل والتوحيد، قالوا: لو كان الله هو الخالق لفعل العبد لكان تعذيبه للعبد على المعاصي ظلما لا عدلا، قال أهل السنة: يعذبه عليها كما يثيبه على الطاعة، لما له فيهما من الكسب والاختيار، فلا ظلم، لكن المعتزلة لم ينظروا في التوحيد تمام النظر، ولم يتبصروا في أدلته تمام التبصر. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 52
1. (1) . His statement "he would not be arguing against them": it suffices for the argument that God is the creator of them and of their acts, in the idols and others, and the idols create nothing; rather, sole creatorship is stronger evidence of sole divinity. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «لم يكن محتجا عليهم» يكفى في الاحتجاج أن الله هو الخالق لهم ولأعمالهم في الأصنام وغيرها، والأصنام لا تخلق شيئا، بل الانفراد بالخالقية أدل على الانفراد بالالهية. (ع)
24
Q 37:97–98 · Vol. 4, p. 52

Verses 97 to 98

The verses as the commentary quotes them
They said, "Build for him a structure and throw him into the Hellfire" (97) And they intended a plot against him, but We made them the lowest (98)
قالُوا ابْنُوا لَهُ بُنْياناً فَأَلْقُوهُ فِي الْجَحِيمِ (97) فَأَرادُوا بِهِ كَيْداً فَجَعَلْناهُمُ الْأَسْفَلِينَ (98)
Vol. 4, p. 52
"Al-jahim" is the fire of intense fuel; it is also said: every fire upon fire and ember upon ember is "jahim." The meaning: God, the Exalted, made him prevail over them in both stations, and humbled them before him: they wanted to defeat him by argument, so God taught him and inspired him with what made them bite the stone, and overcame them, so they inclined to scheming, and God nullified their scheme and made them the humbled, the lowest, who could not overcome him.
الْجَحِيمِ النار الشديدة الوقود، وقيل: كل نار على نار وجمر فوق جمر، فهي جحيم. والمعنى: أن الله تعالى غلبه عليهم في المقامين جميعا، وأذلهم بين يديه: أرادوا أن يغلبوه بالحجة فلقنه الله وألهمه ما ألقمهم به الحجر، وقهرهم فمالوا إلى المكر، فأبطل الله مكرهم وجعلهم الأذلين الأسفلين لم يقدروا عليه.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 52
1. (1) . His statement "he would not be arguing against them": it suffices for the argument that God is the creator of them and of their acts, in the idols and others, and the idols create nothing; rather, sole creatorship is stronger evidence of sole divinity. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «لم يكن محتجا عليهم» يكفى في الاحتجاج أن الله هو الخالق لهم ولأعمالهم في الأصنام وغيرها، والأصنام لا تخلق شيئا، بل الانفراد بالخالقية أدل على الانفراد بالالهية. (ع)

Q 37:99–101 · Vol. 4, pp. 52–53

Verses 99 to 101

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me (99) My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous" (100) So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy (101)
وَقالَ إِنِّي ذاهِبٌ إِلى رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ (99) رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (100) فَبَشَّرْناهُ بِغُلامٍ حَلِيمٍ (101)
Vol. 4, p. 52
By his going to his Lord he meant: his emigrating to where he was commanded to emigrate, from the land of Syria, as He said:
أراد بذهابه إلى ربه: مهاجرته إلى حيث أمره بالمهاجرة إليه من أرض الشام، كما قال:
Vol. 4, p. 53
"I am emigrating to my Lord." "He will guide me": He will direct me to what is good for my religion and protect me and grant me success, as Moses ﷺ said: "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me" — as if God had promised him and said to him: "I will guide you," so he made his speech follow the pattern of his Lord's promise; or based on God's habit with him in guiding and directing him; or he showed thereby his reliance and his entrusting his affair to God. Had he intended hope and desire he would have said, as Moses ﷺ said: "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way." "Grant me from among the righteous": grant me one of the righteous, meaning a child, because the word "hiba" (gift) predominates in referring to a child, although it has been used for a brother in His saying "And We gave him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet." The Mighty and Majestic said: "And We gave him Isaac and Jacob," "and We gave him Yahya." Ali ibn Abi Talib said to Ibn Abbas ؓ when he congratulated him on his son Ali, father of kings: "You have thanked the Giver, and may you be blessed in what was given." For that reason names were given such as Hibatullah, Mawhub, Wahb and Mawhib. The good tidings contained three things: that the child is a male boy, that he reaches the age of maturity, and that he will be forbearing; and what forbearance is greater than his when his father presented slaughter to him and he said: "You will find me, if God wills, among the patient," then submitted to it. It is said: God did not describe the prophets, peace be upon them, with anything less than He described them with forbearance, because of the rarity of its existence. God described Abraham with it in His saying "Indeed, Abraham was compassionate and forbearing," and "Indeed Abraham was forbearing, compassionate, and repentant," because the event bore witness to the forbearance of both.
إنى مهاجر إلى ربى. سَيَهْدِينِ سيرشدنى إلى ما فيه صلاحي في دينى ويعصمني ويوفقني، كما قال موسى عليه السلام كَلَّا إِنَّ مَعِي رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ كأن الله وعده وقال له: سأهديك، فأجزى كلامه على سنن موعد ربه. أو بناء على عادة الله تعالى معه في هدايته وإرشاده. أو أظهر بذلك توكله وتفويضه أمره إلى الله. ولو قصد الرجاء والطمع لقال، كما قال موسى عليه السلام عَسى رَبِّي أَنْ يَهْدِيَنِي سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ. هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ هب لي بعض الصالحين، يريد الولد، لأنّ لفظ الهبة غلب في الولد وإن كان قد جاء في الأخ في قوله تعالى وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ مِنْ رَحْمَتِنا أَخاهُ هارُونَ نَبِيًّا قال عز وجل وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ إِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ يَحْيى وقال على بن أبى طالب لابن عباس رضى الله عنهم- حين هنأه بولده علىّ أبى الأملاك-: شكرت الواهب، وبورك لك في الموهوب. ولذلك وقعت التسمية بهبة الله، وبموهوب، ووهب، وموهب. وقد انطوت البشارة على ثلاث: على أن الولد غلام ذكر، وأنه يبلغ أوان الحلم، وأنه يكون حليما، وأى حلم أعظم من حلمه حين عرض عليه أبوه الذبح، فقال: ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصابرين، ثم استسلم لذلك. وقيل: ما نعت الله الأنبياء عليهم السلام بأقل مما نعتهم بالحلم، وذلك لعزة وجوده. ولقد نعت الله به إبراهيم في قوله إِنَّ إِبْراهِيمَ لَأَوَّاهٌ حَلِيمٌ، إِنَّ إِبْراهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّاهٌ مُنِيبٌ لأنّ الحادثة شهدت بحلمهما جميعا.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 52

1. (1) . قوله «لم يكن محتجا عليهم» يكفى في الاحتجاج أن الله هو الخالق لهم ولأعمالهم في الأصنام وغيرها، والأصنام لا تخلق شيئا، بل الانفراد بالخالقية أدل على الانفراد بالالهية. (ع)

Q 37:102 · Vol. 4, pp. 53–54

Verse 102

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And when he reached with him the [age of] exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if God wills, among the steadfast" (102)
فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعْيَ قالَ يا بُنَيَّ إِنِّي أَرى فِي الْمَنامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فَانْظُرْ ماذا تَرى قالَ يا أَبَتِ افْعَلْ ما تُؤْمَرُ سَتَجِدُنِي إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ (102)
Vol. 4, p. 53
"When he reached" the age of striving with his father in his tasks and needs.
فلما بلغ أن يسعى مع أبيه في أشغاله وحوائجه.
Question
If you say: To what is "with him" attached?
فإن قلت: مَعَهُ بم يتعلق؟
Answer
I say: it cannot but be attached either to "reached," or to "exertion," or to an omitted word. It cannot be attached to "reached" since that would require their both reaching the limit of exertion, nor to "exertion," because the complement of a verbal noun does not precede it; so what remains is that it is explanatory, as if, when He said "when he reached the exertion," that is, the limit at which he was able to exert himself, it was asked: with whom? and He said: with his father. The sense of specifying the father is that he is the gentlest of people with him and the most tender toward him, while others might treat him harshly in demanding exertion and he would not bear it, because his strength was not yet firm and his sapling had not hardened; and he was then thirteen years old. What is meant: that despite the tenderness of his age and his being within the bounds of childhood, he had in him such steadiness of forbearance and breadth of chest that it emboldened him to bear that great trial and give that wise answer. It came to him in a dream and it was said to him: "Slaughter your son," and the dream of prophets is revelation like revelation in wakefulness; hence he said "I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you," so he mentioned the interpretation of the dream, as the one examined says when he has seen that he is riding in a ship: "I saw in a dream that I am saved from this ordeal." It is also said: on the night of Tarwiya he saw as if a speaker said to him: God commands you to slaughter
قلت: لا يخلو إما أن يتعلق ببلغ، أو بالسعي، أو بمحذوف، فلا يصح تعلفه ببلغ لاقتضائه بلوغهما معا حدّ السعى، ولا بالسعي لأنّ صلة المصدر لا تتقدم عليه، فبقى أن يكون بيانا، كأنه لما قال: فلما بلغ السعى أى الحدّ الذي يقدر فيه على السعى قيل: مع من؟ فقال مع أبيه. والمعنى في اختصاص الأب أنه أرفق الناس به، وأعطفهم عليه، وغيره ربما عنف به في الاستسعاء فلا يحتمله، لأنه لم تستحكم قوته ولم يصلب عوده، وكان إذ ذاك ابن ثلاث عشرة سنة. والمراد: أنه على غضاضة سنه وتقلبه في حد الطفولة، كان فيه من رصانة الحلم وفسحة الصدر ما جسره على احتمال تلك البلية العظيمة والإجابة بذلك الجواب الحكيم: أتى في المنام فقيل له: اذبح ابنك، ورؤيا الأنبياء وحى كالوحى في اليقظة، فلهذا قال إِنِّي أَرى فِي الْمَنامِ أَنِّي أَذْبَحُكَ فذكر تأويل الرؤيا، كما يقول الممتحن وقد رأى أنه راكب في سفينة: رأيت في المنام أنى ناج من هذه المحنة، وقيل: رأى ليلة التروية كأن قائلا يقول له: إنّ الله يأمرك بذبح
Vol. 4, p. 54
this son of yours; so when morning came he reflected from morning till evening: was this vision from God or from Satan? Hence it was called the Day of Tarwiya (reflection); and when evening came he saw the same, and knew that it was from God; hence it was called the Day of 'Arafa (knowledge); then he saw the like of it on the third night, so he resolved to slaughter him, and so the day was called the Day of Nahr (sacrifice). It is also said: when the angels gave him the good news of a forbearing boy, he said: "Then he is God's sacrifice." So when he was born and reached the age of exertion with him, it was said to him: "Fulfil your vow." "So see what you think": of opinion, by way of consultation. It has also been read "madha tara" «1», that is, what do you see of your own opinion and express. And "madha tura" in the passive, that is: what opinion does your soul show you. "Do what you are commanded": that is, what you are commanded to do, the preposition omitted as in the poet's line: "I commanded you the good, so do what you were commanded" «2», or "your command" with the verbal noun annexed to the object, and the thing commanded being named "command." It has also been read "ma tu'maru bihi."
ابنك هذا، فلما أصبح روّى في ذلك من الصباح إلى الرواح، أمن الله هذا الحلم أو من الشيطان؟ فمن ثم سمى يوم التروية، فلما أمسى رأى مثل ذلك، فعرف أنه من الله، فمن ثم سمى يوم عرفة، ثم رأى مثله في الليلة الثالثة، فهم بنحره فسمى اليوم يوم النحر. وقيل: إنّ الملائكة حين بشرته بغلام حليم قال: هو إذن ذبيح الله. فلما ولد وبلغ حد السعى معه قيل له: أوف بنذرك فَانْظُرْ ماذا تَرى من الرأى على وجه المشاورة. وقرئ: ماذا ترى «1» ، أى: ماذا تبصر من رأيك وتبديه. وماذا ترى، على البناء للمفعول، أى: ماذا تريك نفسك من الرأى افْعَلْ ما تُؤْمَرُ أى ما تؤمر به، فحذف الجار كما حذف من قوله: أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به «2» أو أمرك على إضافة المصدر إلى المفعول، وتسمية المأمور به أمرا. وقرئ: ما تؤمر به.
Question
If you say: Why did he consult him in a matter that was decreed by God?
فإن قلت: لم شاوره في أمر هو حتم من الله؟
Answer
I say: He did not consult him to return to his opinion and counsel, but to know what he had regarding the trial of God that had come upon him, so as to firm up his foothold and make him patient if he were to panic, and to be assured of his safety from slipping if he were patient and submitted; and to make him know, so that he would examine his own soul, settle it and make it easy for it, and meet the trial as if at ease with it, and earn reward by submission to God's command before its arrival; and because taking him by surprise «3» with slaughter is regarded as distasteful; and so that it would be a precedent in consultation, for it was said: Had Adam consulted the angels about eating from the tree, that would not have been committed by him.
قلت: لم يشاوره ليرجع إلى رأيه ومشورته، ولكن ليعلم ما عنده فيما نزل به من بلاء الله، فيثبت قدمه ويصبره إن جزع، ويأمن عليه الزلل إن صبر وسلم، وليعلمه حتى يراجع نفسه فيوطنها ويهون عليها، ويلقى البلاء وهو كالمستأنس به، ويكتسب المثوبة بالانقياد لأمر الله قبل نزوله: ولأنّ المغافصة «3» بالذبح مما يستسمج، وليكون سنة في المشاورة، فقد قيل: لو شاور آدم الملائكة في أكله من الشجرة لما فرط منه ذلك.
Question
If you say: Why was that in a dream and not in wakefulness?
فإن قلت: لم كان ذلك بالمنام دون اليقظة؟
Answer
I say: as Joseph ﷺ was shown the prostration of his parents and brothers to him in a dream without revelation to his father, and as the Messenger of God ﷺ was promised entry into the Sacred Mosque in a dream, and other dreams of the prophets, and that is to strengthen the evidence that they are truthful and believed, because the state is either the state of wakefulness or of dreaming, so when both states combine to attest truthfulness, that is stronger as evidence than either alone.
قلت: كما أرى يوسف عليه السلام سجود أبويه وإخوته له في المنام من غير وحى إلى أبيه، وكما وعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دخول المسجد الحرام في المنام، وما سوى ذلك من منامات الأنبياء، وذلك لتقوية الدلالة على كونهم صادقين مصدوقين، لأنّ الحال إما حال يقظة أو حال منام، فإذا تظاهرت الحالتان على الصدق كان ذلك أقوى للدلالة من انفراد أحدهما.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 4, p. 54
1. (1) . His statement "and it was read madha tara": perhaps with damma on the ta' and kasra on the ra', from "arahu yurihi"; so let it be checked. (Ayn)
2. . The explanation of this line of evidence was given in Part Two, page 590; consult it if you wish. End of the corrector's note.
3. . His statement "al-mughafasa": in al-Sihah: "ghafastu the man" means I took him unawares. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «وقرئ ماذا ترى» لعله بضم التاء وكسر الراء، من أراه يريه، فليحرر. (ع)
2. . تقدم شرح هذا الشاهد بالجزء الثاني صفحة 590 فراجعه إن شئت اه مصححه.
3. . قوله «المغافصة» في الصحاح: غافصت الرجل، أى: أخذته على غرة. (ع)
27
Q 37:103–111 · Vol. 4, pp. 54–58

Verses 103 to 111

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead (103) We called to him, "O Abraham (104) You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus We reward the doers of good (105) Indeed, this was the clear trial (106) And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice (107) And We left for him [a good reputation] among later generations (108) Peace upon Abraham (109) Thus We reward the doers of good (110) Indeed, he was of Our believing servants (111)
فَلَمَّا أَسْلَما وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ (103) وَنادَيْناهُ أَنْ يا إِبْراهِيمُ (104) قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيا إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ (105) إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ الْبَلاءُ الْمُبِينُ (106) وَفَدَيْناهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ (107) وَتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرِينَ (108) سَلامٌ عَلى إِبْراهِيمَ (109) كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ (110) إِنَّهُ مِنْ عِبادِنَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (111)
Vol. 4, p. 55
One says: "salima li-amri God," "aslama," and "istaslama" with one meaning. All have been read, meaning he submitted to it and was humbled. Their origin is from your saying: "salima this to so-and-so" when it became solely his. Its meaning: it became free of being disputed over; and their saying "salima li-amri God" and "aslama lahu" are transferred from it, and the truth of their meaning is: he devoted himself purely to God and made it sound and exclusive for Him; likewise the meaning of "istaslama": he took his soul purely for God. From Qatada on "aslama": this one surrendered his son and this one himself. "And he put him down upon his forehead (jabin)": he laid him on his side, so one of his two temples fell upon the earth, in agreement «1» on undertaking the command with patience and fortitude, to please the Most Merciful and disgrace Satan. It is reported that this was at the rock in Mina; and from al-Hasan: at the place overlooking the Mosque of Mina. From al-Dahhak: at the slaughtering place where sacrifice is performed today.
يقال: سلم لأمر الله، وأسلم، واستسلم بمعنى واحد. وقد قرئ بهنّ جميعا إذا تنقاد له، وخضع، وأصلها من قولك: سلم هذا لفلان إذا خلص له. ومعناه: سلم من أن ينازع فيه، وقولهم: سلم لأمر الله، وأسلم له منقولان منه، وحقيقة معناهما: أخلص نفسه لله وجعلها سالمة له خالصة، وكذلك معنى: استسلم: استخلص نفسه لله. وعن قتادة في أَسْلَما أسلم هذا ابنه وهذا نفسه وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ صرعه على شقه، فوقع أحد جبينيه على الأرض تواضعا «1» على مباشرة الأمر بصبر وجلد، ليرضيا الرحمن ويخزيا الشيطان. وروى أن ذلك كان عند الصخرة التي بمنى، وعن الحسن: في الموضع المشرف على مسجد منى. وعن الضحاك: في المنحر الذي ينحر فيه اليوم.
Question
If you say: Where is the answer to "when"?
فإن قلت: أين جواب لما؟
Answer
I say: it is omitted, its implication being: "when they submitted and he laid him on his forehead, and We called to him, 'O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision,' what happened happened, which the situation expresses and description cannot encompass, of their rejoicing and delight, their praise of God and gratitude to Him for what He bestowed on them, of removal of the great trial after it had come, and what they gained within it, by settling their souls to it, of reward and compensations and God's good pleasure beyond which there is nothing more to seek"; and His saying "Indeed, thus We reward the doers of good" is an explanation for His granting them what He granted of relief after hardship and attainment of the aim after despair. "The clear trial": the manifest testing in which the sincere are distinguished from others; or the trial of manifest difficulty, than which there is no harder trial. "Dhibh" is the name of what is slaughtered. From Ibn Abbas ؓ both: it was the ram that Abel offered and it was accepted from him, and it had been grazing in Paradise until Ishmael was ransomed by it. From al-Hasan: he was ransomed by an ibex «2» sent down to him from Thabir. From Ibn Abbas: Had that sacrifice been completed, it would have become the custom and people would have slaughtered their sons. «3» "Great": large of body, fat, and that is the Sunna for sacrificial animals; and his saying ﷺ: "Choose well your sacrificial animals, for they are your mounts over the Bridge." It is also said: because it came as a ransom for the son of Abraham. It is reported that it fled from Abraham ﷺ at the Jamra, so he threw seven pebbles at it until he caught it, so stoning remained a custom. It is reported that he stoned Satan when he exposed himself to him with whispering at the slaughter of his son. It is reported that when he slaughtered it Gabriel said: God is greatest, God is greatest; and the sacrificed one said: There is no god but God and God is greatest; and Abraham ﷺ said: God is greatest and to God belongs praise «4»; so it remained a custom. In the story of the sacrificed one it is related that when he wanted to slaughter him he said: "O my son, take the rope and the knife and go with us to the ravine to gather firewood." When he was in the middle of the ravine of Thabir he told him what he was commanded, and he said: "Tighten my bonds so I do not thrash about, and draw back your garments
قلت: هو محذوف تقديره: فلما أسلما وتله للجبين وَنادَيْناهُ أَنْ يا إِبْراهِيمُ قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيا كان ما كان مما تنطق به الحال ولا يحيط به الوصف من استبشارهما واغتباطهما، وحمدهما لله وشكرهما على ما أنعم به عليهما، من دفع البلاء العظيم بعد حلوله، وما اكتسبا في تضاعيفه بتوطين الأنفس عليه من الثواب والأعواض ورضوان الله الذي ليس وراءه مطلوب، وقوله إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ تعليل لتخويل ما خوّلهما من الفرج بعد الشدّة، والظفر بالبغية بعد اليأس الْبَلاءُ الْمُبِينُ الاختبار البين الذي يتميز فيه المخلصون من غيرهم. أو المحنة البينة الصعوبة التي لا محنة أصعب منها. الذبح: اسم ما يذبح. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما: هو الكبش الذي قرّبه هابيل فقبل منه، وكان يرعى في الجنة حتى فدى به إسماعيل. وعن الحسن: فدى بو على «2» أهبط عليه من ثبير. وعن ابن عباس: لو تمت تلك الذبيحة لكانت سنة وذبح الناس أبناءهم» عَظِيمٍ ضخم الجثة سمين، وهي السنة في الأضاحى. وقوله عليه السلام «استشرفوا ضحاياكم فإنها على الصراط مطاياكم» وقيل: لأنه وقع فداء عن ولد إبراهيم. وروى أنه هرب من إبراهيم عليه السلام عند الجمرة فرماه بسبع حصيات حتّى أخذه، فبقيت سنة في الرمي. وروى أنه رمى الشيطان حين تعرض له بالوسوسة عند ذبح ولده: وروى أنه لما ذبحه قال جبريل: الله أكبر الله أكبر، فقال الذبيح: لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر، فقال إبراهيم عليه السلام: الله أكبر ولله الحمد «4» ، فبقى سنة: وحكى في قصة الذبيح أنه حين أراد ذبحه وقال: يا بنى خذ الحبل والمدية وانطلق بنا إلى الشعب نحتطب، فلما توسط شعب ثبير أخبره بما أمر، فقال: اشدد رباطى لا أضطرب، واكفف عنى ثيابك
Vol. 4, p. 56
so that none of my blood splashes on them, which would diminish my reward and my mother would see it and grieve; and sharpen your blade and pass it quickly over my throat to finish me off, so that it will be easier, for death is hard; and recite my greeting to my mother, and if you see fit to return my shirt to my mother, do so, for perhaps it will be easier for her." Abraham ﷺ said: "How excellent a helper you are, my son, in God's command." Then he turned to him kissing him, having bound him, both of them weeping, then put the knife on his throat and it did not cut, because God had set a plate of copper over his throat. He said to him: "Lay me on my face, for if you look at my face you will have pity on me and a tenderness will overcome you that will come between you and God's command." So he did, then he put the knife on his nape and the knife turned over, and a call came: "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision." He looked, and behold, Gabriel ﷺ was with a white-spotted horned ram; so Gabriel and the ram and Abraham and his son said "God is greatest," and he went to the slaughtering place of Mina and slaughtered it. It is also said: when the place of his prostration reached the ground, the relief came. Abu Hanifa ؒ cited this verse regarding one who vows to slaughter his son: that he is obliged to slaughter a sheep.
لا ينتضح عليها شيء من دمى فينقص أجرى وتراه أمى فتحزن، واشحذ شفرتك وأسرع إمرارها على حلقى حتى تجهز علىّ، ليكون أهون فإنّ الموت شديد، واقرأ على أمى سلامى، وإن رأيت أن تردّ قميصي على أمى فافعل، فإنه عسى أن يكون أسهل لها، فقال إبراهيم عليه السلام: نعم العون أنت يا بنىّ على أمر الله، ثم أقبل عليه يقبله وقد ربطه، وهما يبكيان، ثم وضع السكين على حلقه فلم تعمل. لأنّ الله ضرب صفيحة من نحاس على حلقه، فقال له: كبني على وجهى فإنك إذا نظرت وجهى رحمتني وأدركتك رقة تحول بينك وبين أمر الله، ففعل، ثم وضع السكين على قفاه فانقلب السكين، ونودي: يا إبراهيم قد صدقت الرؤيا، فنظر فإذا جبريل عليه السلام معه كبش أقرن أملح، فكبر جبريل والكبش، وإبراهيم وابنه، وأتى المنحر من منى فذبحه: وقيل: لما وصل موضع السجود منه إلى الأرض جاء الفرج. وقد استشهد أبو حنيفة رحمه الله بهذه الآية فيمن نذر ذبح ولده: أنه يلزمه ذبح شاة،
Question
If you say: Which of his two sons was the sacrificed one?
فإن قلت: من كان الذبيح من ولديه؟
Answer
I say: there is disagreement about it. From Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and a group of the Successors: it was Ishmael. The argument for it is that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I am the son of the two sacrificed ones," and a Bedouin said to him: "O son of the two sacrificed ones," and he smiled; he was asked about that and said: When Abd al-Muttalib dug the well of Zamzam he vowed to God that if God made its matter easy for him he would sacrifice one of his sons, and the lot fell on Abd God, but his maternal uncles prevented him and said to him: Ransom your son with a hundred camels; so he ransomed him with a hundred camels; and the second is Ishmael. «1» From Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi he said: the most devout of the Children of Israel used to say when he prayed: "O God, God of Abraham, Ishmael and Israel." Moses ﷺ said: O Lord, why does the most devout of the Children of Israel say when he prays: "O God, God of Abraham, Ishmael and Israel," while I am in their midst, You have made me hear Your speech and chosen me for Your message? He said: O Moses, no one ever loved Me as Abraham loved Me, and he was never given a choice between Me and anything but he chose Me. As for Ishmael, he was generous with his own blood. And as for Israel, he never despaired of My relief in any hardship that befell him. And what indicates it is that God, the Exalted, when He completed the story of the sacrificed one, said: "And We gave him good tidings of Isaac as a prophet." From Muhammad ibn Ka'b: he said to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: It is Ishmael. Umar said: This is something I had not looked into, and I see it as you say; then he sent for a Jew who had become Muslim and asked him, and he said: The Jews know that it is Ishmael, but they envy you Arabs. And what indicates it is that the two horns of the ram were hung in the Ka'ba in the hands of the sons of Ishmael until the House burned. From al-Asma'i he said: I asked Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' about the sacrificed one and he said: O Asma'i, where has your mind strayed? When was Isaac in Makkah? It was Ishmael who was in Makkah, and he is the one who built the House with his father, and the slaughtering place is in Makkah.
قلت: قد اختلف فيه، فعن ابن عباس وابن عمر ومحمد بن كعب القرظي وجماعة من النابعين: أنه إسماعيل. والحجة فيه أنّ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال «أنا ابن الذبيحين» وقال له أعرابى: يا ابن الذبيحين، فتبسم، فسئل عن ذلك فقال: إنّ عبد المطلب لما حفر بئر زمزم نذر لله: لئن سهل الله له أمرها ليذبحن أحد ولده، فخرج السهم على عبد الله فمنعه أخواله وقالوا له أفد ابنك بمائة من الإبل ففداه بمائة من الإبل والثاني إسماعيل» «1» وعن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: كان مجتهد بنى إسرائيل يقول إذا دعا: اللهم إله إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسرائيل، فقال موسى عليه السلام: يا رب، ما لمجتهد بنى إسرائيل إذا دعا قال: اللهم إله إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسرائيل، وأنا بين أظهرهم فقد أسمعتنى كلامك واصطفيتني برسالتك؟ قال: يا موسى، لم يحبني أحد حب إبراهيم قط، ولا خير بيني وبين شيء قط إلا اختارني. وأمّا إسماعيل فإنه جاد بدم نفسه. وأمّا إسرائيل، فإنه لم ييأس من روحي في شدّة نزلت به قط، ويدل عليه أنّ الله تعالى لما أتم قصة الذبيح قال: وَبَشَّرْناهُ بِإِسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا وعن محمد بن كعب أنه قال لعمر بن عبد العزيز: هو إسماعيل، فقال عمر: إنّ هذا شيء ما كنت أنظر فيه، وإنى لأراه كما قلت، ثم أرسل إلى يهودى قد أسلم فسأله، فقال: إن اليهود لتعلم أنه إسماعيل، ولكنهم يحسدونكم معشر العرب، ويدل عليه أن قرني الكبش كانا منوطين في الكعبة في أيدى بنى إسماعيل إلى أن احترق البيت. وعن الأصمعى قال: سألت أبا عمرو بن العلاء عن الذبيح فقال: يا أصمعى أين عزب عنك عقلك، ومتى كان إسحاق بمكة، وإنما كان إسماعيل بمكة، وهو الذي بنى البيت مع أبيه، والمنحر بمكة.
Vol. 4, p. 57
And among what indicates it is that God, the Exalted, described him with patience, apart from his brother Isaac, in His saying "And Ishmael and Idris and Dhul-Kifl, each was of the patient," and that is his patience in being slaughtered; and described him with truthfulness of promise in His saying "Indeed, he was true to his promise," because he promised his father patience from himself in being slaughtered and fulfilled it; and because God gave him good news of Isaac and of his son Jacob in His saying "So she laughed, and We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob"; so had the sacrificed one been Isaac it would have been a breach of the promise regarding Jacob. From Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Mas'ud, al-Abbas, Ata', Ikrima and a group of the Successors: it was Isaac. The argument for it is that God, the Exalted, informed about His intimate friend Abraham, when he emigrated to Syria, that he asked Him to grant him a child, then followed that with the good news of a forbearing boy, then mentioned his dream of slaughtering that boy who was announced. And indicating it is the letter of Jacob to Joseph: "From Jacob Israel of God, son of Isaac the sacrifice of God, son of Abraham the intimate friend of God." «1» If you say: Revelation came to Abraham, God's blessings upon him, in a dream to slaughter his son and he did not slaughter, and it was said to him "you have fulfilled the vision," but he would have fulfilled it only if the slaughter had been completed, and it was not completed «2»
ومما يدل عليه أنّ الله تعالى وصفه بالصبر دون أخيه إسحاق في قوله وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ وهو صبره على الذبح، ووصفه بصدق الوعد في قوله إِنَّهُ كانَ صادِقَ الْوَعْدِ لأنه وعد أباه الصبر من نفسه على الذبح فوفى به، ولأن الله بشره بإسحاق وولده يعقوب في قوله فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْناها بِإِسْحاقَ وَمِنْ وَراءِ إِسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ فلو كان الذبيح إسحاق لكان خلفا للموعد في يعقوب. وعن على بن أبى طالب وابن مسعود والعباس وعطاء وعكرمة وجماعة من التابعين: أنه إسحاق. والحجة فيه أن الله تعالى أخبر عن خليله إبراهيم حين هاجر إلى الشام بأنه استوهبه ولدا، ثم أتبع ذلك البشارة بغلام حليم، ثم ذكر رؤياه بذبح ذلك الغلام المبشر به. ويدل عليه كتاب يعقوب إلى يوسف: من يعقوب إسرائيل الله بن إسحاق ذبيح الله ابن ابراهيم خليل الله «1» . فإن قلت: قد أوحى إلى إبراهيم صلوات الله عليه في المنام بأن يذبح ولده ولم يذبح، وقيل له: قد صدقت الرؤيا، وإنما كان يصدقها لو صح منه الذبح، ولم يصح «2»
Vol. 4, p. 58
I say: He exerted his capacity and did what the slaughterer does: laying him on his side and passing the blade over his throat; but God, glory be to Him, brought what prevented the blade from going through him, and this does not impugn the act of Abraham ﷺ; do you not see that he is not called disobedient or negligent, but is called obedient and diligent, as if the blade had gone through him and cut the jugular veins and let the blood flow; and this is not a case of abrogation occurring to the commanded act before the deed, nor before the time of the deed in anything, as occurs to some minds, such that they busy themselves with speech about it.
قلت. قد بذل وسعه وفعل ما يفعل الذابح: من بطحه على شقه وإمرار الشفرة على حلقه، ولكن الله سبحانه جاء بما منع الشفرة أن تمضى فيه، وهذا لا يقدح في فعل إبراهيم عليه السلام، ألا ترى أنه لا يسمى عاصيا ولا مفرطا، بل يسمى مطيعا ومجتهدا، كما لو مضت فيه الشفرة وفرت الأوداج وأنهرت الدم، وليس هذا من ورود النسخ على المأمور به قبل الفعل، ولا قبل أوان الفعل في شيء، كما يسبق إلى بعض الأوهام، حتى يشتغل بالكلام فيه.
Question
If you say: God, the Exalted, is the one from whom the ransom is paid, since He is the One who commanded the slaughter, so how can He be the ransomer such that He said "And We ransomed him"?
فإن قلت: الله تعالى هو المفتدى منه: لأنه الآمر بالذبح، فكيف يكون فاديا حتى قال وَفَدَيْناهُ؟
Answer
I say: the ransomer is Abraham ﷺ and God, the Mighty and Majestic, gave him the ram to ransom with; and He said "and We ransomed him" only by attributing the ransoming to the cause that made the ransom possible, by His giving.
قلت: الفادي هو إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام، والله عز وجل وهب له الكبش ليفدى به وإنما قال وَفَدَيْناهُ إسنادا للفداء إلى السبب الذي هو الممكن من الفداء بهبته.
Question
If you say: If what Abraham did of laying him down and passing the blade was in the ruling of slaughter, then what is the meaning of ransom, since ransom is only freeing from slaughter with a substitute?
فإن قلت: فإذا كان ما أتى به إبراهيم من البطح وإمرار الشفرة في حكم الذبح. فما معنى الفداء، والفداء إنما هو التخليص من الذبح ببدل؟
Answer
I say: it was known, by God's prevention, that the reality of slaughter did not occur, of cutting the jugular veins and flowing of blood, so God gave him the ram so that its slaughter would stand in the place of that reality, so that this reality would not occur in Ishmael himself but in the ram's self instead of him.
قلت: قد علم بمنع الله أن حقيقة الذبح لم تحصل من فرى الأوداج وانهار الدم، فوهب الله له الكبش ليقيم ذبحه مقام تلك الحقيقة حتى لا تحصل تلك الحقيقة في نفس إسماعيل، ولكن في نفس الكبش بدلا منه.
Question
If you say: What benefit is there in that reality occurring, when it was dispensed with by what Abraham did standing in the place of slaughter without deficiency?
فإن قلت: فأى فائدة في تحصل تلك الحقيقة، وقد استغنى عنها بقيام ما وجد من إبراهيم مقام الذبح من غير نقصان؟
Answer
I say: the benefit in that is that what was prevented be found in its substitute so that fulfilment of the vow and doing of what was commanded be completed from every aspect.
قلت: الفائدة في ذلك أن يوجد ما منع منه في بدله حتى يكمل منه الوفاء بالمنذور وإيجاد المأمور به من كل وجه.
Question
If you say: Why was it said here "Thus We reward the doers of good" and in other stories "Indeed, thus"?
فإن قلت: لم قيل هاهنا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ وفي غيرها من القصص: إنا كذلك؟
Answer
I say: "Indeed, thus" had already come earlier in this story, so it was as though He found it light to drop it, being content with mentioning it once rather than mentioning it a second time.
قلت: قد سبقه في هذه القصة: إنا كذلك، فكأنما استخف بطرحه اكتفاء بذكره مرة عن ذكره ثانية.
